You pasted those three lines into the terminal instead of saving them to a file. In the shell, `POSTGRES_DB=inara` only sets a shell variable. It isn't exported and Compose never reads it, so you get the same warnings.

**Create the file** from your project directory (`~/Projects/inara`):

```bash
cat > .env << 'EOF'
POSTGRES_DB=inara
POSTGRES_USER=inara
POSTGRES_PASSWORD=choose-a-strong-password
EOF
```

Or open it in an editor (`nano .env`) and paste the three lines there.

**Check that Compose sees it:**

```bash
ls -la .env
docker compose config | grep POSTGRES
```

The values should now show `inara` and your password instead of blanks. If they don't, the file is in the wrong directory or has the wrong name.

**Then reset and start.** The failed runs already created the Postgres volume, so wipe it once so Postgres initializes with the new credentials:

```bash
docker compose down -v
docker compose up -d
```

If the warnings disappear but Postgres still exits, run `docker compose logs postgres` and paste the output, since that will show the actual error.

# The local dev database (docs/[local-dev.md](http://local-dev.md)) is built FROM schema.prisma, so pulling from it has

# nothing to sync and only reorders relation fields. Skip the pull there; everything else still runs.

if node scripts/local-db-guard.mjs; then\
echo "⏭ DATABASE_URL is the local dev database; skipping prisma db pull (see docs/[local-dev.md](http://local-dev.md))."\
else\
echo "🔄 Running prisma db pull to ensure schema sync..."\
npx prisma db pull\
echo "🔄 Running prisma db pull to ensure schema sync..."\
npx prisma db pull

# Check for changes in schema.prisma using git status --porcelain

if ! git diff --quiet prisma/schema.prisma; then\
echo "❌ Schema was out of sync! I have updated prisma/schema.prisma."\
echo "⚠️ Please stage the changes (git add prisma/schema.prisma) and commit again."\
exit 1\
fi

echo "✅ Schema is in sync."
